title: Agent Trajectories as Evidence for Software Quality Assurance
abstract: arXiv:2611.22323v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Autonomous software agents increasingly plan, implement, and test software with limited human oversight. Their decisions may introduce implicit assumptions that final code and passing tests do not adequately expose. We propose analyzing observable agent trajectories alongside software and agent specifications and AI generated artifacts as evidence for targeted quality assurance. The aim is to prioritize consequential decisions for scrutiny, investigate their possible contribution to software problems, and inform improvements to specifications and development practices. Industrial experience motivates the idea; available execution records and preliminary analysis methods make it plausible. However, trajectories alone do not establish that decisions are justified, outcomes acceptable, or corrective changes effective. We ask how this evidence can support review, diagnosis, and continuous quality improvement, and when simpler QA approaches

translated_title: 智能体轨迹作为软件质量保证的证据
translated_abstract: 自主软件智能体在极少人工监督的情况下，越来越多地承担软件的规划、实现与测试工作。它们的决策可能引入最终代码和通过的测试无法充分暴露的隐式假设。我们提出将可观察的智能体轨迹，连同软件与智能体规格说明以及AI生成的产物一同分析，作为针对性质量保证的证据。其目标是优先审查那些影响重大的决策，调查它们对软件问题可能产生的作用，并为改进规格说明和开发实践提供依据。工业界的经验激发了这一想法；现有的执行记录和初步分析方法使其具备可行性。然而，仅凭轨迹并不能证明决策是合理的、结果是可接受的，或纠正性修改是有效的。我们探讨这种证据如何支持评审、诊断和持续的质量改进，以及何时采用更简单的质量保证方法……
tldr: 该论文提出将智能体轨迹与规格说明及AI生成产物结合分析，作为针对性软件质量保证的证据，以优先审查智能体影响重大的决策、暴露隐式假设并持续改进开发实践。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes analyzing observable agent trajectories, alongside specifications and AI-generated artifacts, as evidence for targeted software quality assurance—prioritizing scrutiny of consequential agent decisions to expose implicit assumptions and drive continuous improvement.
